_README: Error rates for the rules that decide what the Index publishes. Each was measured against a hand-judged sample drawn by seeded shuffle; `npm run validate -- --full` redraws the same samples. Intervals are Wilson 95%.

overExclusion.how: full census of every withdrawn domain; homepage fetched, title and description read by hand
overExclusion.note: This is the classifier's own rate, which is what it should be: all 4 are corrected in classification-overrides.json, so the shipped pipeline removes none of them today. Checking this turned up that 2 of the 4 — dragonball-super.com and strikerreport.com — had their verdict fixed but were never put back in the audit list, so their report pages were live while they stayed out of the ranking and out of every weekly run. Both are now in submitted.txt and rejoin at the next run.

asShipped.note: after overrides. The 4 raw errors are the measure of the model, not of what the site publishes.

found: az24.vn — a Vietnamese lottery-results site, found on the second draw and now excluded in classification-overrides.json
underExclusion.how: Three draws of 66: `npm run probe-filter`, `SEED=1337 npm run probe-filter` on pool 71275ca25efe, and `npm run probe-filter` again on pool e15d222a8342 after az24.vn was excluded. 176 distinct domains, 156 judged. The rule for 'unreadable' is printed at the top of every run, so it travels with the output.
underExclusion.pools: 71275ca25efe (1,176 kept) for the first two draws, e15d222a8342 (1,175) for the third — excluding az24.vn changed pool membership, which changed the draw, which is exactly what the fingerprint is for.
underExclusion.tiers: 133 judged on the page itself, 23 on robots/sitemap only, 20 on nothing.
underExclusion.sampling: Pseudo-random with a fixed seed over the whole kept pool, not a convenience sample. The pool is sorted to canonicalise the order the shuffle acts on; sorting fixes the order, it does not select.

wholePopulationBound.how: the far edge: the one hand-verified error, plus all 20 domains that stayed unreadable, plus all 23 judged only from robots.txt and sitemap.xml, counted as wrong keeps. URL paths say what a site is made of but are not the page, so a bound leaning on them is not the far edge.
wholePopulationBound.says: at the far edge of the interval, at most 31.9% of kept domains are wrongly kept. Nothing weaker covers the whole sample.
wholePopulationBound.intermediate: Counting only the unresolved as wrong and trusting the robots/sitemap tier: 21/176 = 11.9%, 95% CI 7.9-17.6%.

underExclusion.handJudged: 18 flags across the three draws, one upheld. az24.vn was judged from the site's own title ("Ket qua xo so ba mien" — three-region lottery results). The rest were rejected: CSS and JS tokens leaking through the scan (xxx-large, data-[slot=icon], js-slot), Las Vegas hotel listings on travel sites (kayak.com, priceline.com), a bingo link in a tabloid's games nav (mirror.co.uk), portal Jackpot games (gmx.net, libero.it, web.de), OnlyFans headlines (infobae.com, foxnews.com), a betting-app extradition story (rediff.com), hotels near casinos in a sitemap (skyscanner.net), and polybuzz.ai's own FAQ saying it bans public NSFW.
underExclusion.sensitivity: livescore.com is the closest call and was kept: its title and purpose are live football scores and the rule judges primary purpose, but it sells betting-affiliate placement. Counted as an error too, the rate is 2/156 = 1.3%, 95% CI 0.4-4.6%.
underExclusion.reproducibility: The earlier 0/121 was drawn from the leaderboard in score order, so each weekly run reshuffled the pool and the same seed drew a different sample — reproducible in name only, and it failed silently. The pool is now sorted and fingerprinted, the fingerprint prints on every run and is recorded here, and POOL_HASH=<hash> turns a changed pool into a loud mismatch. Two consecutive runs of seed 2026 on one pool drew the identical 66 domains; one domain's live fetch differed between them (gamma.app), and the conservative run is what is published.
underExclusion.supersedes: 0/44 readable CI 0-8.0%; the single-seed 0/61; and 0/121 CI 0-3.1%, whose pool no longer exists. The honest reading of all three is not that the filter was clean and then broke, but that the draw which would have found az24.vn had not been made yet.

inSample.how: seed 42, 15 sites x 4 categories — the set the rule was tuned against, so not evidence of accuracy

heldOut.how: seed 99, disjoint from seed 42, 10 readable sites x 4 categories
heldOut.note: SUPERSEDED as the current rate by heldOutPostFix. Retained because it is what the rule scored before clarin.com and grow.google were fixed.

heldOutPostFix.how: seed 777, disjoint from seeds 42 and 99; 14 readable sites x 4 categories, judged by hand
heldOutPostFix.note: measured after the clarin.com and grow.google fixes. Pre-fix on seed 99 the held-out rate was 10%.
heldOutPostFix.checked: mega.nz 0/20 and bankofamerica.com 5/20 looked like under-credits and were verified correct: mega.nz serves a one-word JS shell, bankofamerica.com links no privacy page from its homepage HTML.

falsePositive.note: three detections is too few to support a rate; each was hand-checked against platform runtime config, not the detector's own patterns

shopMembership.how: seed 11, 20 domains marked shop, judged by hand
shopMembership.boundary: A shop is a site whose primary purpose is selling goods or services to the public and where a visitor can start a purchase. News, reference, social, government, sport, banking and free tools are not shops even when they sell a subscription. Whether to narrow this to retail only is a product decision, not a measurement one.
